items.title: Nepal’s push for mountain climate action features in COP31 draft decision
items.summary: The proposal calls for a dedicated programme on mountain regions and climate change, with the issue set to become a regular item on future COP agendas.

items.title: Opposition urges PM to forge national consensus before India visit
items.summary: Leaders say Prime Minister Shah should prioritise restoring trust and resolving longstanding disputes over border, treaties, trade, hydropower, and air routes.

items.title: Nvidia rules out Huang comeback as campaign for his return grows
items.summary: More than 180,000 people have signed a petition calling for the former chief executive’s reinstatement, but the board is not considering bringing him back.

items.title: Nepal’s stolen heritage in focus at ‘Bring Me Home’ festival in Bhaktapur
items.summary: The fest, which also features an exhibition, brings renewed attention to Nepal’s looted religious artefacts and the communities still waiting for their return.

items.title: Dipendra Singh Airee carries Sudurpaschim’s hope for the maiden title
items.summary: Sudurpaschim Royals, the two-time finalists, have another shot for their maiden NPL title in the third season. And they face their toughest challenger, Lumbini Lions, in Qualifier 1.

items.title: Deuba’s rival convention plan raises questions over Congress’ legitimacy
items.summary: Despite the Election Commission and Supreme Court recognising Gagan Thapa’s leadership, Sher Bahadur Deuba’s camp is preparing its own 15th general convention, citing a pending court review.

items.title: Is Nepal’s new Parliament building ready for winter session move-in?
items.summary: Seven years after construction began, and with the main contract extended six times, the House chamber still awaits tests and handover.

items.title: If Chhath is for everyone, why are Dalit devotees still pushed to the edge of the pond?
items.summary: Constitutional guarantees mean little until communities and local governments enforce them.

items.title: When institutions fade, democracy follows
items.summary: Reform means making institutions more accountable to their objectives, not moulding them to suit the new convenience of power.

items.title: Gen Z is on the streets everywhere. What do they want?
items.summary: From Kathmandu to Delhi to Belgrade, young protesters share anger over corruption and prices, but little else in the way of organisation or leaders.

items.title: Saudi employers face Rs4m fines for allowing workers to take outside jobs
items.summary: The Interior Ministry has warned individual employers against letting workers work for others or independently.

items.title: For NPL cheerleaders, cold nights, catcalls and modest pay
items.summary: Three performers share the untold realities of entertaining Kirtipur crowds.

items.title: Sudurpaschim coach Misbah-ul-Haq meets Pakistan ambassador
items.summary: The former Pakistan captain met Mohammad Aamir Khan in Kathmandu, where the embassy hosted a dinner in his honour.

items.title: How India’s delay is set to leave Rs135m of Nepal’s electricity unsold daily
items.summary: A separate 40MW seasonal export arrangement with Bangladesh has also expired, leaving the power utility with surplus electricity it cannot sell abroad and putting millions in daily revenue at risk.

items.title: Air routes, economic package top agenda for Shah’s India visit
items.summary: Several contentious issues between the two neighbours are unlikely to see any substantive progress during the state visit.

items.title: Why is Tatopani border still closed? Stakeholders say it’s time Kathmandu asked Beijing
items.summary: Traders and local representatives want the government to seek an explanation from China and secure a lasting arrangement for the operation of the key trade route.

items.title: Dayahang Rai is back in box-office spotlight
items.summary: With ‘Kabaddi 5’ and ‘Pension Patta’ turning into commercial hits, Rai is once again proving his draw—and his enduring place in films rooted in indigenous stories.

items.title: Beyond Ghorepani, tourists are discovering Parbat’s village life
items.summary: Homestays, traditional food, folk music and scenic walking trails are drawing trekkers to settlements that offer a closer look at rural life.

items.title: New Indian envoy calls on Nepal’s foreign minister
items.summary: Ambassador Sudhakar Dalela meets Shisir Khanal at Singha Durbar and discusses the longstanding ties between the two countries.

items.title: Four of a family killed in Bajhang auto-rickshaw crash
items.summary: Vehicle plunges 900 metres off a hillside in Bungal Municipality; 13-year-old boy survives unharmed as police detain driver.

items.title: Bhutanese rights groups urge Shah to raise refugee issue with India
items.summary: They want the prime minister to press Narendra Modi to help resolve the decades-old refugee crisis, secure the release of political prisoners and address human rights violations in Bhutan.

items.title: Nepal’s ambassadors to India, China and Israel take oath
items.summary: The three were among ten ambassadorial nominees approved by the Parliamentary Hearing Committee after the Cabinet recommended 13 appointments in September.

items.title: Deleted from India’s voter rolls, some Muslims face detention, deportation
items.summary: A voter-roll revision has become entangled with a wider crackdown on suspected undocumented migrants.

items.title: Night travel restricted on Hetauda-Kathmandu road via Bhimphedi
items.summary: The move follows a fatal crash that killed 14 people last week, with authorities citing the narrow, winding and poorly lit road as a major accident risk.

items.title: Six wild elephants die in two months, raising conservation concerns
items.summary: From Chitwan to eastern Nepal, a series of elephant deaths has alarmed conservationists, who warn that shrinking habitats, human activities and unsafe migration routes could threaten the country’s wild elephant population.
